newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet may review gasoline quota tomorrow.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet may review gasoline quota tomorrow.

text.p: The Polish government is likely to discuss introducing a duty-free gasoline import quota when it discusses the fuel market tomorrow, the government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said on Monday.

She said the government would analyse reports that some regions may face temporary shortages, notably of diesel, which producers and distributors say may take place due to high world oil prices and domestic caps on gasoline prices.
"(The government meeting) may be a good opportunity to discuss whether it is reasonable to introduce a duty-free import quota earlier," Jakubowska told a news briefing.

The industry ministry has asked the government to approve a duty-free quota for imports of 300,000 tonnes of gasoline but Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said the quota need not be introduced immediately, but later -- simultaneously with the planned liberalisation of gasoline prices.

The finance ministry, which controls fuel prices, opposes their quick liberalisation, fearing it would jeopardise plans to curb inflation to 17 percent in December this year from 21.6 percent in 1995.

But Polish refineries and distributors complain that world oil prices and official limits on price increases make production and imports increasingly less profitable and are pressing the government to allow prices to rise.
Poland's second biggest refinery in Gdansk has already said it will cut output in September. Domestic refineries can cover 80 percent of demand for fuels in Poland.

PAP news agency reported that supplies of diesel fuels have temporarily dried up in the southwestern province of Kalisz and that the neighbouring province of Wroclaw might face such shortages on Tuesday.

The Polish Liquid Fuels Chamber, a private distributors' group, which strongly lobbies for duty-free quotas and price liberalisation, said some 300,000 tonnes of gasoline and 400,000 tonnes of diesel were needed to stabilise the market.
Poland's largest refinery, Petrochemia Plocka, urged the government on Tuesday to use the state reserves to offset possible shortages but Jakubowska said she did not think this was necessary.
Also the state-owned CPN fuels distributor, Poland's largest chain, said fuels were available nationwide.
